commands.description: One batched read of host, OS, the server's own IPv4 (source address of its route to the internet) and its Tailscale IPv4 (empty when Tailscale is not installed or connected), uptime, load, CPU counters, memory, disks and reboot flag and the names of unhealthy containers (empty if docker is absent). Sections start with a '##name' line.
commands.script: echo '##hostname'; hostname; echo '##os'; cat /etc/os-release; echo '##uptime'; cat /proc/uptime; echo '##loadavg'; cat /proc/loadavg; echo '##nproc'; nproc; echo '##stat'; head -1 /proc/stat; echo '##meminfo'; grep -E '^(MemTotal|MemAvailable):' /proc/meminfo; echo '##df'; df -P -B1 -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs -x squashfs -x overlay 2>/dev/null; echo '##system'; echo "vendor=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null)"; echo "product=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null)"; echo "machine_id=$(cat /etc/machine-id 2>/dev/null)"; echo "kernel=$(uname -r)"; echo "boot_id=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id 2>/dev/null)"; echo "time=$(date '+%s %z %Z')"; echo "ip=$(ip -4 route get 1.1.1.1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /^src$/){print $(i+1); exit}}')"; T=$(timeout 3 tailscale ip -4 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$T" ] || T=$(ip -4 -o addr show dev tailscale0 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d/ -f1 | head -1); echo "tailscale_ip=$T"; echo '##reboot'; if [ -f /var/run/reboot-required ]; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; U=$(apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null); echo '##updates'; echo "$U" | grep -c -E '^[^/ ]+/'; echo '##security'; echo "$U" | grep -c -E '^[^/ ]+/[^ ]*-security'; echo '##unhealthy'; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy --format '{{.Names}}' 2>/dev/null

commands.description: All containers (docker ps -a) plus one-shot resource stats for running ones. Compose stacks are derived from container labels.
commands.script: echo '##docker'; if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ok; else echo missing; fi; echo '##ps'; docker ps -a --format '{{json .}}' 2>&1; echo '##stats'; docker stats --no-stream --format '{{json .}}' 2>&1

commands.description: docker start one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker start {id}

commands.description: docker stop one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker stop {id}

commands.description: docker restart one container. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker restart {id}

commands.description: Follow one container's logs, starting with the last 100 lines. Run over a pseudo-terminal on its own connection; stop by sending Ctrl-C. {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker logs -f --tail 100 {id}

commands.description: Packages apt can upgrade (from the local package cache; no root, no network), held packages, when the cache was last refreshed, and whether a reboot is pending.
commands.script: echo '##apt'; if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo ok; else echo missing; fi; echo '##upgradable'; apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null; echo '##held'; apt-mark showhold 2>/dev/null; echo '##refreshed'; stat -c %Y /var/lib/apt/periodic/update-success-stamp 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y /var/lib/apt/lists 2>/dev/null; echo '##reboot'; if [ -f /var/run/reboot-required ]; then echo yes; else echo no; fi

commands.description: docker compose pull for one stack: downloads newer images, changes no containers. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} pull

commands.description: docker compose up -d for one stack: recreates only containers whose image or config changed, starts stopped ones. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} up -d

commands.description: docker compose restart for one stack: restarts every container without recreating it. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order. All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell.
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} restart

commands.description: docker compose up -d --build for one stack: rebuilds images for services with a build section (from their Dockerfiles), then recreates the containers whose image or config changed. Services that only use pulled images are untouched. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order. All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell.
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} up -d --build

commands.description: docker compose up -d --build --no-deps for ONE service of a stack: rebuilds that service's image from its Dockerfile and recreates its container if it changed; its dependencies and the other services are untouched. {service} must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ and be a service of the stack (from the container's compose service label). Other placeholders as in compose_rebuild.
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} up -d --build --no-deps {service}

commands.description: docker compose up -d --force-recreate for one stack: recreates every container. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {dir} is the project's working directory, and {files} is `-f <path>` once per compose file, in label order (compose merges them in that order). All paths are absolute, from the project's labels, single-quoted for the shell (' becomes '\'').
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} up -d --force-recreate

commands.description: apt-get update: refresh the package lists. Installs nothing. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get update

commands.description: apt-get upgrade: install every available upgrade. Never installs new packages or removes any, and held packages stay. Keeps existing config files. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get upgrade -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold

commands.description: apt-get install --only-upgrade for the named packages only (used for security updates). {packages} is a space-separated list; at most 200 names, each must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]+$. Runs as root, or through `sudo -n` (never prompts) for other users; it fails with sudo's message if that is not allowed.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LC_ALL=C apt-get install --only-upgrade -y -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold {packages}

commands.description: Interactive shell in one container, run as the remote command of an ssh -t terminal tab (not through the transport). {id} must match ^[0-9a-f]{12,64}$.
commands.script: docker exec -it {id} sh -c 'if command -v bash >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec bash; else exec sh; fi'

commands.description: Read one file of a stack (a compose file or <working_dir>/.env): missing, too large (over 65536 bytes), or its mtime, mode, owner, sha256 and base64 content. Read only. {file} is the quoted absolute path.
commands.script: F={file}; if [ ! -e "$F" ]; then echo '##missing'; exit 0; fi; if [ "$(stat -c %s "$F")" -gt 65536 ]; then echo '##toolarge'; exit 0; fi; echo '##meta'; stat -c '%Y %a %U:%G' "$F"; echo '##sha256'; sha256sum "$F" | cut -d' ' -f1; echo '##content'; base64 -w0 "$F"; echo

commands.description: Check new content for one stack file without changing anything: writes it to a temp file in the stack's folder and runs docker compose config -q with the temp file standing in for the edited file (or as --env-file for .env). Exit 0 = valid; otherwise the output holds compose's errors (e.g. 'yaml: line 5: ...'); exit 7 = the folder is not writable. {args} is -f for every compose file with the edited one replaced by "$T". All paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell; {b64} is the file content base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: D={dir}; T=$(mktemp "$D/.rackoon-check.XXXXXX") || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -f "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T"; docker compose -p {project} --project-directory "$D" {args} config -q 2>&1

commands.description: Save new content over one stack file: refuses if the file's sha256 no longer matches what was opened (exit 3, ##changed; {expect} is that check, or a not-exists check for a new file), validates with docker compose config (exit 4, ##invalid, nothing written), copies the old file to <file>.rackoon.bak, keeps owner and mode, then moves the new file into place atomically (##saved and the new sha256). Exit 7 = not writable. All paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell; {b64} is the file content base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: F={file}; D={dir}; {expect}; T=$(mktemp "$D/.rackoon-save.XXXXXX") || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -f "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T"; if ! OUT=$(docker compose -p {project} --project-directory "$D" {args} config -q 2>&1); then echo '##invalid'; echo "$OUT"; exit 4; fi; if [ -e "$F" ]; then chmod --reference="$F" "$T"; chown --reference="$F" "$T" 2>/dev/null; cp -p "$F" "$F.rackoon.bak" || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; else chmod 600 "$T"; fi; mv -f "$T" "$F"; echo '##saved'; sha256sum "$F" | cut -d' ' -f1

commands.description: Check a NEW stack's files without creating anything in its real folder: writes compose.yaml (and .env, when {env} is the .env step) into a scratch folder from mktemp -d, runs docker compose config -q there, and removes the scratch folder on exit. {b64} is the compose file base64-encoded and quoted; {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$. {env} is empty or `echo <base64> | base64 -d > "$T/.env"; `. Exit 7 = cannot create the scratch folder.
commands.script: T=$(mktemp -d) || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$T/compose.yaml"; {env}cd "$T" && docker compose -p {project} config -q 2>&1

commands.description: Create a new stack: refuses if {dir} already exists (exit 3, ##exists), creates {parent} if needed and then {dir} (exit 7 = not writable), writes compose.yaml (and .env with mode 600 when {env} is the .env step: `echo <base64> | base64 -d > "$D/.env" && chmod 600 "$D/.env" || exit 7; `, otherwise empty), checks it in place with docker compose config -q (exit 4, ##invalid), and on any failure removes the files and the folder it made. Success prints ##created. {dir} is <parent>/<name>; all paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell. {b64} is the compose file base64-encoded and quoted.
commands.script: D={dir}; P={parent}; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo '##exists'; exit 3; fi; mkdir -p "$P" && mkdir "$D" || { echo '##cannot-write'; exit 7; }; ok=; trap '[ -n "$ok" ] || { rm -f "$D/compose.yaml" "$D/.env"; rmdir "$D" 2>/dev/null; }' EXIT; echo {b64} | base64 -d > "$D/compose.yaml" || exit 7; {env}if ! OUT=$(cd "$D" && docker compose -p {project} config -q 2>&1); then echo '##invalid'; echo "$OUT"; exit 4; fi; ok=1; echo '##created'

commands.description: Does the image exist in its registry, as seen from the server (so private registries it is logged in to work)? Prints found, timeout (20 s) or notfound; notfound also covers a registry that needs a login. {image} is a validated image name (letters, digits and . _ / : @ -), single-quoted.
commands.script: timeout 20 docker manifest inspect {image} >/dev/null 2>&1; case $? in 0) echo found;; 124) echo timeout;; *) echo notfound;; esac

commands.description: TCP ports with a listener on the server, one line per socket: the fourth column is the local address and the port follows its last colon. Used to tell whether a host port is free before adding a container.
commands.script: ss -H -tln 2>/dev/null

commands.description: Delete a stack: docker compose down --remove-orphans stops and removes its containers and the networks compose made (images are never removed). {volumes} is empty or ` -v` (also remove the named volumes the compose file declares). {folder} is empty, or the folder step: ` && cd / && { [ -f {file} ] || { echo '<missing>'; exit 6; }; } && { [ ! -L {dir} ] || { echo '<symlink>'; exit 6; }; } && R=$(readlink -f -- {dir}) && { case "$(readlink -f -- {file})" in "$R"/*) true;; *) echo '<outside>'; exit 6;; esac; } && { rm -rf -- {dir} || { [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] && sudo -n rm -rf -- {dir}; } || { echo '<permissions>'; exit 6; }; }`. It runs only after down succeeded. Each guard has its own message and exit 6: the compose file is missing, the folder is itself a symlink, or the compose file's real path is not inside the folder's real path (a symlinked parent folder is fine and is deleted through); sudo -n is the second try for files a container created as root. The app offers it only for a folder that is not a system tree, mount point or home folder and that holds every compose file of the stack. {project} must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$; all paths are absolute and single-quoted for the shell.
commands.script: cd {dir} && docker compose -p {project} {files} down --remove-orphans{volumes}{folder}

commands.description: The kernel's boot id: a random id that changes on every boot. Used after a reboot to tell the server has really restarted, not just kept its old connection.
commands.script: cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id

commands.description: Reboot the server in 2 seconds (so this ssh command can return and close cleanly). Runs as root or through sudo -n; if sudo would ask for a password it exits 5 with ##no-sudo and nothing is scheduled. The reboot is started with nohup so it survives the session ending.
commands.script: if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then S=; else S='sudo -n'; fi; $S true || { echo '##no-sudo'; exit 5; }; nohup sh -c "sleep 2; $S systemctl reboot" >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null & echo '##rebooting'

commands.description: Wraps an action's command to stream its output live: stty sets the pty to the terminal that will show it ({cols}x{rows}), the command runs in a subshell, and its exit code is printed as a final ##rackoon-exit:<n> line (a streamed ssh gives output but no exit status). Used with a pty (ssh -tt) so docker compose draws its normal progress.
commands.script: stty cols {cols} rows {rows} 2>/dev/null; ( {command} ); rk=$?; echo; echo "##rackoon-exit:$rk"

commands.description: List one folder for the Files screen. {dir} is an absolute path, single-quoted. Exit 3: the folder doesn't exist; exit 4: it isn't readable. Output is NUL separated: the folder's real path (symlinks resolved), then eight fields per entry: type (f d l ...), type after following a link (d for a link to a folder, N broken), size in bytes, modified as epoch seconds, permissions as ls prints them, owner, name, link target (empty unless a link). Needs GNU find. NUL separation keeps any file name intact. The app shows at most 5000 entries.
commands.script: cd -P -- {dir} 2>/dev/null || exit 3; [ -r . ] && [ -x . ] || exit 4; printf '%s\0' "$PWD"; find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -printf '%y\0%Y\0%s\0%T@\0%M\0%u\0%f\0%l\0' 2>/dev/null

commands.description: The ssh user's home folder as an absolute real path, where the Files screen starts.
commands.script: pwd -P

commands.description: Upload one file: the content arrives on stdin. {dest} and {tmp} are absolute single-quoted paths (tmp is `.<name>.rackoon-part` beside dest) and {bytes} is the exact size being sent. Written to tmp first and moved into place only if tmp is exactly {bytes} long (a cancelled or dropped upload looks like a normal end of input to cat, so without the check a half file would be moved into place); an existing file keeps its owner and mode; a folder with that name is refused (exit 5).
commands.script: D={dest}; T={tmp}; if [ -d "$D" ]; then echo 'A folder with that name already exists.' >&2; exit 5; fi; cat > "$T" || { rm -f -- "$T"; exit 1; }; if [ "$(wc -c < "$T")" -ne {bytes} ]; then rm -f -- "$T"; echo 'The upload was interrupted, so nothing was changed.' >&2; exit 1; fi; if [ -e "$D" ]; then chmod --reference="$D" "$T" 2>/dev/null; chown --reference="$D" "$T" 2>/dev/null; fi; mv -f -- "$T" "$D" || { rm -f -- "$T"; exit 1; }

commands.description: Upload a folder: a tar stream on stdin holding {src}/... is received into a scratch folder ({tmpdir}, a mktemp template inside the destination folder), checked to be exactly {bytes} long (else nothing is touched, exit 1), unpacked, then moved to {dest}; if {dest} is already a folder its contents are merged in. Files are owned by the ssh user (--no-same-owner). The scratch folder is always removed.
commands.script: T=$(mktemp -d {tmpdir}) || exit 1; mkdir "$T/x"; cat > "$T/in.tar"; if [ "$(wc -c < "$T/in.tar")" -ne {bytes} ]; then echo 'The upload was interrupted, so nothing was changed.' >&2; rc=1; else tar -xf "$T/in.tar" -C "$T/x" --no-same-owner; rc=$?; if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then if [ -d {dest} ]; then cp -a -- "$T"/x/{src}/. {dest}/; else mv -- "$T"/x/{src} {dest}; fi; rc=$?; fi; fi; rm -rf -- "$T"; exit $rc

commands.description: Download one file: the content leaves on stdout. {path} is absolute and single-quoted.
commands.script: cat -- {path}

commands.description: Download a folder as a tar stream of its contents on stdout. {path} is the absolute single-quoted folder; tar changes into it, which follows a symlink to a folder (links inside stay links). The app unpacks it into a folder named after the entry.
commands.script: tar -C {path} -cf - .

commands.description: Create one folder. {path} is absolute and single-quoted. Refuses a name that is taken (exit 5); never creates parents.
commands.script: if [ -e {path} ] || [ -L {path} ]; then echo 'That name is already taken.' >&2; exit 5; fi; mkdir -- {path}

commands.description: Rename or move within one folder. {from} and {to} are absolute single-quoted paths. Refuses when {to} exists (exit 5).
commands.script: if [ -e {to} ] || [ -L {to} ]; then echo 'That name is already taken.' >&2; exit 5; fi; mv -- {from} {to}

commands.description: Delete one file, or a symlink itself (a link is never followed).
commands.script: rm -f -- {path}

commands.description: Delete a folder and everything in it. Offered only for folders that are not system trees, mount points, home folders or shallower than three levels (checked by the app and again before the command is built).
commands.script: rm -rf -- {path}
